friend.name: Mo the Mower
friend.look: a cute green toy lawn mower with big friendly eyes and a yellow handle

plan.label: Loud or sudden sounds
helps: hear the sound first at home in the story
ask: a quiet room or the first or last appointment of the day
a warning before loud tools turn on

plan.label: Being touched by strangers
helps: the grown-up touches first to show
know which body part and for how long
hold the tool first, like the stethoscope
ask: "tell, show, do": say it, show it on a toy, then do it
the parent doing simple steps like the thermometer
plan.src: Tell-show-do technique, American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry

pages.text: I go to the barber. I see big chairs!
pages.say: Ooooh! Look, Leo! The barber shop. We go inside. What do you see?
pages.scene: A child and their grown-up walking into a barber shop with a friendly barber waving at them.

pages.text: I wait for my turn. I sit with my blue blanket.
pages.say: Ahhh! What is that? A waiting chair. You can sit and wait. I wait too. [giggles]
pages.scene: A child sitting in a waiting area with their blue blanket, and a toy lawn mower friend sitting next to them.

pages.text: It is OK to feel worried. My grown-up is there to help me.
pages.say: Hmm... feeling worried? That is OK, Leo. Your grown-up is here. And me too!
pages.scene: The child sits close to their grown-up, who gives a gentle hug. The friend snuggles in too. Calm, soft light.

pages.text: I sit in the big chair. It goes up high!
pages.say: Oh my! Look! The big chair. The big chair! It goes up... up... up! Can you see it?
pages.scene: A child sitting in a barber chair with a toy lawn mower friend beside them, both looking up at the ceiling.

pages.text: A cape goes on me. It keeps me clean.
pages.say: Hmm... what do I see? A cape! It goes around you. Like a big hug. Can you feel it?
pages.scene: A barber putting a cape around a child, with a toy lawn mower friend watching and wearing a tiny cape.

pages.text: Water sprays my hair. It feels cool!
pages.say: Psst... look over here! Water spray. It's like a little shower. Can you feel it?
pages.scene: A barber spraying water on a child's hair, with a toy lawn mower friend beside them getting sprayed with a tiny water spray.

pages.text: I hear the clippers. They buzz loud!
pages.say: Ooooh! Look, Leo! Clippers. They buzz loud. Like a big lawn mower! Can you hear it? Let's cover our ears and count to 5.
pages.scene: A child covering their ears and a toy lawn mower friend covering its ears, with a barber holding clippers in the background.

pages.text: The clippers touch my hair. They tickle my neck.
pages.say: Hmm... what do I feel? The clippers. They touch your hair. Like a little tickle. Can you feel it? I'm right here.
pages.scene: A barber using clippers on a child's hair, with a toy lawn mower friend watching and looking concerned.

pages.text: Little hairs fall down. They feel itchy!
pages.say: Ahhh! What is that? Little hairs. They fall down. Like little pieces of grass. Can you see them?
pages.scene: A child feeling itchy from little hairs, with a toy lawn mower friend looking itchy and scratching itself.

pages.text: A soft brush wipes them off. It feels nice!
pages.say: Oh my! Look! A soft brush. It wipes the hairs away. Like a little sweep. Can you feel it?
pages.scene: A barber using a soft brush to wipe away little hairs from a child, with a toy lawn mower friend being swept with a tiny brush.

pages.text: I look in the mirror. I see my new haircut!
pages.say: Ooooh! Look, Leo! The mirror. You can see yourself. Like a big reflection. Can you see your new haircut?
pages.scene: A child looking in a mirror and seeing their new haircut, with a toy lawn mower friend looking in a tiny mirror and admiring itself.

pages.text: All done! I get to go home!
pages.say: Hmm... what do I see? We're all done! You can go home now. Like a big finish. Can you say yay?
pages.scene: A child and their grown-up leaving the barber shop, with a toy lawn mower friend waving goodbye.

pages.text: Now it is time for lawn mowers.
pages.say: Guess what? Lawn mowers! Yay... lawn mowers!
pages.scene: The child plays happily with lawn mowers at home, with the friend playing too.
